The Vendetta Gazette

Vol. XIX • August 17, 2026 • “All the Blood That’s Fit to Print” • Two Cents (If You’re Still Alive to Pay)

★ TERRITORY GAINS THIS WEEK ★ Wu-Tang           +229 turfs
Flattop           +107 turfs
Claude            +85 turfs

The Iron Fist Tightens — Wu-Tang Runs Riot Across Vendetta City for the Second Consecutive Week

Two Hundred and Twenty-Nine Turfs Swallowed Whole; Thirteen Headquarters Smashed to Splinters; The Man's Army Now Numbers Five Thousand Souls and Shows No Sign of Stopping By Our Man in the Trenches, Ignatius P. Flambeau

This correspondent confesses, with no small measure of professional humiliation, that last week's edition of this very newspaper dared to characterise Wu-Tang's one-hundred-and-fifty-one turf conquest as the ceiling of one man's ambition. We were wrong. Magnificently, catastrophically, breathtakingly wrong. The Iron Fist of the East Side has returned this week not merely to repeat his performance but to surpass it — seizing two hundred and twenty-nine turfs across Vendetta City in a single seven-day rampage that has left rivals speechless, city cartographers weeping, and your correspondent seriously reconsidering his career in journalism.

Wu-Tang's war machine has grown to a staggering five thousand and forty-six garrison units — a rise of fourteen hundred and twenty-two souls in one week alone. To put that figure in plain language for our more numerically timid readers: the man is not merely winning; he is manufacturing victory on an industrial scale, training and deploying fresh Henchmen, Bouncers, and Enforcers faster than his enemies can count their losses. Thirteen enemy headquarters fell to his assault columns this week, including the unfortunate Psycute, whose command post was overrun not once, not twice, but three times in a single week — a humiliation so thorough that even this seasoned reporter paused to wince in sympathy.

Flattop Finds His Footing — The Flat-Capped Conqueror Claims One Hundred and Seven Turfs

Six HQ Captures and Fifty-Seven Raids Mark the Rise of Vendetta City's Most Industrious Number Two By Our Staff Correspondent

While Wu-Tang commands the headlines with the subtlety of a runaway locomotive, one must not neglect the quietly devastating campaign waged by Flattop — that flat-capped, gimlet-eyed schemer who has now, for two weeks running, established himself as the city's second most dangerous territorial appetite. One hundred and seven turfs seized, six headquarters captured, and fifty-seven raids conducted with the methodical efficiency of a man who keeps ledgers on his enemies' ledgers. His garrison, modest at three hundred and forty-four units compared to the Iron Fist's army, belies a sharpness of strategic instinct that compensates handsomely for the difference in raw numbers.

Most notable among Flattop's conquests this week: the storming of Grandstorm's headquarters on the ninth of August — a coup that sent that once-proud outfit into total dissolution, their fifty-eight turfs stripped away and their garrison reduced to precisely zero. Cakeman's command post fell to Flattop on the same day, that unfortunate operation likewise gutted to nothing. Two empires, one afternoon. The man works fast.

Claude Endures — The Methodical One Adds Eighty-Five Turfs, Plunders GodFather's Vaults

Last Week's Champion Cedes the Pace Crown But Not the War By Our Staff Correspondent

Let no man mistake a temporary demotion to third place for weakness in the case of Claude. Eighty-five new turfs, ten enemy headquarters reduced to rubble, and forty raids conducted with characteristic precision — these are not the numbers of a man in retreat. They are the numbers of a man consolidating, sharpening, and waiting. His garrison has swelled by four hundred and eighty-seven units to a total of seven hundred and seventy-three, suggesting that Claude is not content merely to hold what he has seized but is actively fortifying against the storm he surely sees gathering on the eastern horizon.

The week's most audacious single strike belongs to Claude alone: a raid upon the vaults of GodFather — a figure whose name alone once inspired a respectful lowering of voices in Vendetta City's better speakeasies —
